page: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. The instance provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 192 GB of system memory, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU allocation characteristic of low-memory compute profiles. Local storage consists of a bundled 5,669 GB NVMe SSD, providing direct high-speed scratch space alongside support for premium remote storage.

Benchmark evaluations reflect high parallel throughput, with the multi-core Geekbench score reaching 21,105 and PassMark CPU achieving 86,003.68, both placing in the top decile. Parallel workloads benefit from Intel AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets, demonstrated by strong matrix and vector execution scores. Static web serving throughput reaches 110.74 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression tests achieve 495.7 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing shows read cached speeds exceeding 6,253 GB/sec, though uncached large-block write operations average 106.47 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers economical scaling for tasks bottlenecked on core execution and local IOPS rather than massive memory footprints. The bundled 5.6 TB NVMe drive mitigates the need for supplementary high-tier scratch disks. However, workloads requiring large in-memory caches may face constraints under the 192 GB ceiling relative to the 96 vCPUs. Suitable workloads include build compilation pipelines, web serving clusters, intermediate data processing, high-throughput caching, and parallel scientific batch jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure D96lds_v6 is a high-density compute server featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with clock speeds reaching 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 48 physical cores, it includes 192 GB of system memory and 5,669 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. The hardware is configured with advanced vector extensions, including AVX-512 and AMX, enabling high-throughput parallel execution without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, it achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score (86,003.68) and multi-core Geekbench (21,105), complemented by static web serving output of 110.74 GB/sec. With a 2 GB per vCPU memory profile, this instance provides cost-effective throughput for compute-intensive workloads that rely heavily on fast local storage, such as Clang software compilation, Redis key-value workloads, batch analytics, and distributed web serving tiers.
